Here is how consumers read indexed context:

---

## Single read interface: `@atlas/sdk`

The function is **`createContextSDK`**, exported from `@atlas/sdk` (`packages/sdk/src/context/sdk.ts:1045`). It returns a `ContextSDK` façade — the single read interface every consumer uses. The docs state it explicitly:

> *"This is the single interface consumers use to access repository context — CLI, MCP, editors, and agents must not touch the SQLite database directly."* (`docs/CONTEXT_SDK.md:4-6`)

### Concrete seam a consumer calls

```ts
import { createContextSDK } from "@atlas/sdk";

const context = createContextSDK({ repositoryPath: "/path/to/repo" });
const hits = context.search.search("authentication");
context.close();
```

The returned `ContextSDK` exposes sub-APIs: `files`, `symbols`, `dependencies`, `modules`, `summaries`, `search`, `project`, `write`, plus `status()`, `freshness()`, `getRelevantContext()`, and `refresh()`.

---

## Where persistent context is stored and owned

The database lives at **`<repositoryPath>/.codeatlas/context.db`** (resolved by `resolveContextConfig` in `packages/sdk/src/context/sdk.ts:88-96`, also via `ATLAS_ROOT`/`ATLAS_DB` env vars).

Ownership belongs to **`@atlas/storage`** — specifically the **`ContextStore`** class (`packages/storage/src/context-store.ts:41`), which implements `ContextDatabasePort` and manages all eight tables: Files, Symbols, Dependencies, Summaries, Modules, Relationships, Hashes, Metadata (`packages/storage/src/schema.ts:10-99`).

The SDK opens the store internally via:
```ts
// packages/sdk/src/context/sdk.ts:99-101
function openStore(dbPath: string): ContextDatabasePort | null {
  return existsSync(dbPath) ? new ContextStore({ filePath: dbPath }) : null;
}
```

---

## Dependency direction

Dependencies flow **inward**, enforced by ESLint:

```
Consumer (CLI / MCP / extension)
    ↓ imports only @atlas/sdk
Context SDK (@atlas/sdk)
    ↓ imports @atlas/storage (among others)
ContextStore (@atlas/storage) implements ContextDatabasePort from @atlas/core
    ↓ imports only @atlas/core + @atlas/shared
```

From `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md:31-34`:
- **`sdk`** may import `shared`, `core`, `hashing`, `scanner`, `parser`, `storage`, `graph`, `context`, `cache`, `providers`, `summary`, `search`, `usage`, `agents`.
- **`cli`** may import only `sdk`, `mcp`, `benchmark` — never `@atlas/storage` or `@atlas/search` directly.
- **`mcp`** may import only `sdk`.
- **`@atlas/storage`** may import only `core` + `shared`.

### Concrete consumer call sites

| Consumer | File | How it calls the SDK |
|---|---|---|
| CLI `atlas search` | `apps/cli/src/commands/search.ts:180` | `createContextSDK({ repositoryPath, dbPath, metrics, usage })` |
| CLI `atlas explain` | `apps/cli/src/commands/explain.ts:79` | `createContextSDK({ repositoryPath: root, dbPath, metrics, usage })` |
| MCP server | `packages/mcp/src/context.ts:91` | `createContextSDK({ dbPath, repositoryPath, metrics, usage })` |
| VS Code extension | `apps/extension/src/client.ts:210` | `createContextSDK(this.options)` |

All four reach context exclusively through `@atlas/sdk`'s `createContextSDK`. No consumer imports `@atlas/storage`, `@atlas/search`, or `@atlas/summary` directly — the SDK is the sole read façade.
